title: Logging in an Express service
idea: In a Node.js service the logger becomes middleware: each request gets a child logger carrying its request id, and every line is one JSON object.
points: A child logger adds fields like `requestId` to every line it writes.
One access line per completed request is logged on `finish`; aborted ones need `close`.
Error middleware logs the failure once and returns a safe 500 body.
Interview follow-ups: ship lines centrally, sample DEBUG, carry ids with `AsyncLocalStorage`.

hero.title: One failing request, end to end

messages.label: GET /boom, X-Request-Id
messages.note: A client may send its own request id. The service reuses a short, safe id; otherwise it makes one.

messages.label: req.log = child
messages.note: The middleware binds the id into a child logger and attaches it to `req`.

messages.label: throw Error
messages.note: Express forwards the thrown error to the error middleware; Express 5 also does this for rejected promises from async handlers.

messages.label: error line
messages.note: The error is logged once, with the request id, as one JSON line.

messages.label: 500 + requestId
messages.note: The client gets no stack trace, only an id it can quote to support.

messages.label: request done
messages.note: On `finish`, the access line records method, path and status.

code.title: Logger as middleware
code.caption: A small JSON logger with levels, child loggers and redaction, wired into Express. Lines go to an in-memory appender so the run prints them. Redaction is by key for brevity; production code should allow-list fields.

walk.text: Levels, a memory appender, a fixed clock and a redaction list.
Children share the level state but add bound fields such as `requestId`.
Middleware reuses a short, safe request id or makes one, then logs one access line on finish.
`express.json` runs after `req.log` exists; the route validates with zod and hides DEBUG at INFO.
An admin route changes the shared level at runtime, accepting only known levels.
Error middleware logs the message once and hides details from the client.
Happy path, 400, 500, a bad and a good level change, then a repeat.

pitfalls: Key-based redaction misses nested fields and secrets in messages; prefer an allow-list of fields.
Do not log the same error in the route and the error middleware.
Protect the log-level endpoint; anyone who can set DEBUG can flood your disks.

quiz.q: Which `requestId` appears on the `unhandled error` line?
quiz.why: The client sent `X-Request-Id: edge-42`. The middleware reuses an incoming id, and the child logger stamps it on every line for that request.

takeaway: One JSON line per event, a request id on every line, secrets never.
